sentences.text: The known fossil material includes a shoulder girdle, complete fossilized arms with feathers, some ribs, and gastralia — the internal belly ribs found in some dinosaurs.
Yixianosaurus possessed a very long hand measuring 140% of the length of its 89 mm humerus, where the second finger is the longest among its digits and bears large, recurved claws.
The estimated total body length of Yixianosaurus is 1 meter and its weight is 1 kilogram.
Its hand was exceptionally long, measuring 140% of the length of its humerus.
The fingers of Yixianosaurus bear large and recurved claws, a feature often associated with grasping or climbing.
A partial skeleton of Yixianosaurus was discovered in 2001 at Wangjiagou in Liaoning, northeastern China.
Researchers suggest that large pennaceous feathers on the forelimbs indicate Yixianosaurus was adapted for limited aerial locomotion.
Yixianosaurus is classified within the unranked family Maniraptora.
It is also classified within the family Anchiornithidae.
A 2017 re-evaluation determined that Yixianosaurus was the most basal paravian.
The original describers suggested Yixianosaurus was a close relative of the Scansoriopterygidae.
Yixianosaurus lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, 122 million years ago during the Aptian, in what is now Asia.
The time range for Yixianosaurus is estimated from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
Some researchers have suggested that Yixianosaurus may belong to the dromaeosaurid group.
It is debated whether Yixianosaurus is a primitive dinosaur outside the Eumaniraptora clade or a basal member of the Paraves.
